newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican navy burns one tonne of cocaine.
newsitem.headline: Mexican navy burns one tonne of cocaine.

text.p: Keen to show results in the drug war ahead of a U.S. decision on whether it is a reliable anti-narcotics ally, the Mexican Navy on Thursday burned 1.1 tonnes of confiscated cocaine and other drugs before reporters in the holiday resort of Cozumel.
Admiral Alberto Del Barrio Guille, commander of the naval district that includes the Yucatan coastline, looked on as sailors poured gasoline over the heap of cocaine and set it ablaze with a torch.
Smaller amounts of marijuana and hallucinogenic pills were also burned.

Officials said the cocaine was found abandoned about 15 days ago on the small island of Punta Pajaros, not far from the resort of Cancun, where hundreds of thousands of foreign tourists flock each year to soak up the Caribbean sun.

The burning ceremony, in a field within the naval base of Cozumel, 800 miles (1,280 km) southeast of Mexico City, came as the U.S. government decided whether to certify Mexico as an ally in the drug war.
Del Barrio told reporters that his sailors, working with other law enforcement authorities, had confiscated a total of five tonnes of cocaine over the past two years in the area.
Anti-drug agents say tonnes of drugs are shipped by sea each year from the Yucatan peninsula to the northern Mexican border states, for smuggling into the United States.
